title: UNet 3+: A Full-Scale Connected UNet for Medical Image Segmentation (classification-guided module)
mechanism: An image-level presence classifier on the deepest features multiplies the segmentation output, removing over-segmentation in negative images.
adaptation: Two binary heads, inactive-present and crack-present, trained with BCE on mask-derived labels (42 inactive-positive train cells). Use a soft gate (p_seg x p_img) so that one missed cell does not zero its whole mask. Keep the val-chosen threshold.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + presence heads with soft gate (hard gate as a second setting). Baseline: PF. Metrics: inactive precision and IoU (CV and clean 49), E1 inactive IoU. Kill if the inactive IoU gain is < 0.02 or the inactive recall drop is > 0.03.
evidence: R: the abstract says the module reduces over-segmentation in non-organ images, on 2 datasets. The abstract page gives no numbers.

alt_notes.adaptation: Two binary heads (inactive-present, crack-present), soft gate p_seg(inactive) x p_img(inactive); 42 positive cells so soft gate only, val-chosen threshold kept.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + presence heads, soft gate vs hard gate; baseline PF; metrics inactive precision and IoU (CV), E1 inactive IoU; kill if inactive CV IoU gain < 0.02.
